sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content: • **Tinkathia System**: A colonial agrarian practice requiring tenants to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their landholding. • **The Catalyst**: Raj Kumar Shukla, a local cultivator, persuaded Gandhi to visit Champaran at the 1916 Lucknow Session of the INC. • **The Method**: Gandhi employed 'Satyagraha' (truth-force) and 'Ahimsa' (non-violence) to challenge the legal and social hegemony of the planters. • **The Outcome**: The Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) abolished the Tinkathia system and provided partial compensation to farmers.

items.definition: A compulsory contract system where 3 out of 20 parts of land were reserved for indigo, often on the most fertile soil, leading to soil exhaustion and food insecurity.
A government-appointed committee including Gandhi as a member, which recommended the abolition of the Tinkathia system, marking a rare victory for peasant agitation.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content: • **Social Upliftment**: Gandhi established schools and sanitation programs in villages to address the 'constructive work' aspect of the movement. • **Fact-Finding Mission**: Gandhi conducted a massive survey of thousands of peasants to build a legal and moral case against the planters.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content: • **Key Challenges**: Resistance from local administration and the threat of expulsion under Section 144. • **Solutions**: Strategic use of legal documentation and public pressure to force the government to negotiate.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content: • **Memory Acronym**: 'C-A-R-E' (Champaran, Agrarian, Rajendra/Raj Kumar, End of Tinkathia). • **Decoded Meaning**: C (Champaran), A (Agrarian issue), R (Raj Kumar Shukla/Rajendra Prasad), E (End of Tinkathia).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the year (1917) with the Champaran Agrarian Act (1918). Also, note that Gandhi was NOT the first to raise the issue; local leaders had been protesting for years.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Constructive Programme' to describe Gandhi's focus on education and sanitation during the movement, showing his holistic approach to nation-building.

keyTakeaways: Champaran was the first successful application of Satyagraha in India.
It shifted the focus of the national movement towards the agrarian peasantry.
The movement established Gandhi as a pan-Indian leader with a unique mass-mobilization strategy.
